topic: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Requirements Engineering (RE): A Systematic Literature Review
topic_definition: Stage 1 observable projection of the original paper's eligibility. Use title and abstract evidence to judge whether the study is a primary empirical work applying LLMs or prompting to Requirements Engineering tasks.
summary: Stage 1 title/abstract projection of source-faithful Stage 2 criteria; publication-time fallback filtering is handled by cutoff_jsons/2509.11446.json.

summary_topics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Requirements Engineering (RE): A Systematic Literature Review

required.criterion: Title/abstract indicates use of large language models, LLMs, ChatGPT, GPT models, prompt engineering, prompt tuning, or closely related generative prompting methods.

Title/abstract indicates support for Requirements Engineering tasks, such as elicitation, analysis, specification, modeling, validation, verification, management, traceability, classification, or requirements documents.

Title/abstract indicates a primary study with empirical evaluation, experiment, case study, benchmark, user study, tool evaluation, or dataset evaluation, or leaves empirical sufficiency plausible enough for Stage 2 confirmation.

exclusion_criteria.criterion: Title/abstract clearly indicates the work uses LLMs but not to support Requirements Engineering tasks.
Title/abstract clearly indicates a secondary study, tertiary study, systematic review, mapping study, survey, or literature review.
Title/abstract clearly indicates a conceptual, perspective, or opinion paper without empirical evaluation.
